subject: Physics
chapter: Newton's Laws of Motion and Friction

raw.questionText: A block $A$ of mass $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ is placed on a smooth horizontal surface. Block $A$ has a vertical guide slot in which a block $C$ of mass $m_3 = 1\text{ kg}$ can slide freely without friction, meaning block $C$ can only move vertically relative to block $A$. Another block $B$ of mass $m_2 = 1\text{ kg}$ is placed on the flat horizontal top surface of block $A$. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between block $A$ and block $B$ are $\mu_s = 0.3$ and $\mu_k = 0.2$, respectively. A light, inextensible string connects block $B$ to block $C$ over a light, frictionless pulley fixed at the top-right corner of block $A$. The system is released from rest with the horizontal segment of the string taut. Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: The acceleration of block $A$ is $\frac{8}{7}\text{ m/s}^2$ towards the left.
The tension in the string is $\frac{38}{7}\text{ N}$.
The horizontal force exerted by block $A$ on block $C$ is $\frac{8}{7}\text{ N}$.
The acceleration of block $B$ relative to the ground is $\frac{32}{7}\text{ m/s}^2$ towards the right.
raw.explanation: By analyzing the horizontal center-of-mass constraint and the relative motion of the blocks, we determine that slipping must occur, allowing us to solve the coupled equations of motion.
